vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse/worked-example-round-trips-to-equivalent-osd
vectors.comment: E.14's worked example, the canonical proof case for this extension. Result is expressed as the canonical OSD text write_schema would produce, since record/field declaration order in the OSD-OML source matches OSD's own order (E.7) -- an implementation MAY compare via schema equivalence instead of this exact text, per E.12.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse/cardinality-forms

expect.schema:
record R {
    "a": any,
    "b": any,
    "c" [3]: any,
    "d" [1,5]: any,
    "e" [5,]: any,
    "f" [,5]: any,
    "g" [,]: any,
}
root R

vectors.comment: E.5's full table in one schema: an absent cardinality edge and an empty {} both mean exactly-1 (no cardinality suffix in OSD); every other row maps to its OSD bracket form. Every field also carries an explicit `type: { kind: "any" }` since Field.type is [1,1] (E.8) -- OSD-OML has no field-type-omitted form, unlike cardinality.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse/type-kinds

expect.schema:
record R {
    "a": string,
    "b": string?,
    "c": R,
    "d": any,
}
root R

vectors.comment: E.6: all four Type shapes in one schema -- plain scalar, nullable scalar, a self-ref (mutual recursion is legal per Sec3.3 of the Schema model, inherited unchanged), and any. `nullable` is present as `true` only on field b; its absence elsewhere is what E.6 requires (never present as `false`).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse/empty-record-is-legal
vectors.comment: E.8: Record.field is [0,], so a record with zero field edges (Record.field entirely absent, not an empty array -- OML has no empty-array sugar per Sec4.3.1) is legal, matching OSD's own `record R { }`.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse/record-and-field-order-is-not-significant
vectors.comment: E.7: record/field order carries no meaning -- B is declared before A even though A references B, and B's fields are declared y-then-x. This is a forward-reference case (already legal per the Schema model's Sec3.3) restated in OSD-OML's own record ordering, plus field order within B. Only ok:true is asserted here since the canonical writer's own deterministic-order choice (declaration order) is a writer detail, not part of what this vector is proving; extensions-osd-oml/parse/worked-example-round-trips-to-equivalent-osd already exercises exact-text comparison for order-matching input.
